reasoning: Rubbing two suitable substances creates unlike charges on them, and these charges do not last long. The atmosphere does affect them: moisture in the air carries the charge away, which is why static experiments fail on humid days. So statement C is the false one.

Magnets are made from iron, cobalt, nickel and their alloys such as alnico (aluminium, nickel, cobalt) and ticonal (titanium, cobalt, nickel, aluminium, iron). Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin, which is not magnetic, so the group with bronze cannot be used to make a magnet.

reasoning: (1) A magnet pulls a nail without touching it: non contact force. (2) A floating ball stays at rest because its weight and the upthrust cancel: balanced force. (3) The bat touches the ball: contact force. (4) A stone sinks because its weight is more than the upthrust: unbalanced force.

A black hole packs a huge mass into a tiny space, so its density is extremely high. A red giant is a star whose outer layers have swollen to an enormous size, so its density is very low. White dwarfs and neutron stars are very dense, and the Sun is in between.

reasoning: Everyone has the same number of vocal cords. In men they are longest (about 20 mm), in women shorter (about 15 mm) and in children shorter still. Shorter cords vibrate faster, giving a higher pitch, so the voices differ.

Sodium and aluminium are in the same period. Going across a period the nuclear charge increases and pulls the electrons closer, so atoms get smaller. Sodium comes before aluminium, so the sodium atom is larger.
Diamond and graphite are pure forms (allotropes) of carbon, so carbon is free in them. Marble is calcium carbonate and wool is a protein, so in both the carbon is combined with other elements.

LPG has no smell of its own. A small amount of ethyl mercaptan, which has a strong bad smell, is added so that a leak can be noticed at once.

A metal that gives salt and hydrogen with both an acid and a base (like zinc or aluminium) is amphoteric. It is a metal, so it is electropositive (i true, iv false). Its oxide is amphoteric, showing both basic and acidic nature, so (ii) and (iii) are true.

value: X and Y have different physical properties

Vinegar (pH about 3), black coffee (about 5) and urine (about 6) are all acidic, with pH below 7. Blood has a pH of about 7.4, which is slightly basic, so it is the odd one out.

Water is \(\mathrm{H_2O}\), with two hydrogen atoms for one oxygen atom. In electrolysis oxygen is given off at the anode and hydrogen at the cathode, in the ratio 1 : 2 by volume. So the gas at the anode is half the volume of the gas at the cathode.

Borax is \(\mathrm{Na_2B_4O_7 \cdot 10H_2O}\): 2 sodium, 4 boron and 7 oxygen atoms with 10 molecules of water. Epsom salt is \(\mathrm{MgSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O}\) and Glauber's salt is \(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4 \cdot 10H_2O}\).
In \(\mathrm{XCl_2}\) the metal joins two chloride ions, so X has valency 2. Sulphate has valency 2, giving \(\mathrm{XSO_4}\), and hydroxide has valency 1, giving \(\mathrm{X(OH)_2}\).

LNG and CNG are natural gas, which is mostly methane, and biogas is mostly methane too. LPG is mainly butane and propane, so it is the odd one out.
